Here’s a concise, fact-focused overview of the 2011–12 Harvard Crimson men’s basketball team:

Overview
- Head coach: Tommy Amaker (5th season)
- Home arena: Lavietes Pavilion
- Overall record: 26–5 (program record for wins at the time)
- Ivy League record: 12–2 (Ivy League champions, first outright Ivy title in program history)
- NCAA Tournament: Earned automatic bid; first NCAA appearance since 1946
- NCAA result: Lost in the Round of 64 to Vanderbilt (5-seed) as a 12-seed

Notable Achievements
- First AP Top 25 ranking in program history (entered the poll in December 2011; spent multiple weeks ranked, peaking in the low 20s)
- Won the inaugural Battle 4 Atlantis tournament (notable win over nationally ranked Florida State)
- Set or tied several program bests, including most single-season wins and one of the best starts in school history
- Established Harvard as the Ivy’s national standard-bearer, following a shared title the year before

Key Games/Highlights
- Battle 4 Atlantis: beat Utah, upset ranked Florida State, and won the final (over UCF)
- Non-conference: road loss at nationally ranked UConn; continued local dominance with another win over Boston College
- Ivy race: controlled league play to finish 12–2 and clinch the automatic NCAA bid

NCAA Tournament
- Seed: 12 (East Region)
- Opponent: 5-seed Vanderbilt (SEC Tournament champion)
- Result: Loss, 79–70

Roster Core
- Keith Wright (Sr., F/C) – 2010–11 Ivy Player of the Year; frontline anchor and co-captain
- Kyle Casey (Jr., F) – athletic forward, All-Ivy caliber
- Brandyn Curry (Jr., G) – primary ballhandler/playmaker
- Oliver McNally (Sr., G) – veteran guard, co-captain
- Laurent Rivard (So., G) – top perimeter shooter
- Christian Webster (Jr., G)
- Wesley Saunders (Fr., G/F) – promising two-way wing who later became an Ivy POY
- Frontcourt depth included Steve Moundou-Missi (Fr., F) and Jonah Travis (Fr., F)

Recognition and Context
- Multiple All-Ivy selections (Wright and Casey among them; Curry/McNally also honored)
- Amaker’s group delivered milestone “firsts” for Harvard basketball: first national ranking, first outright Ivy title, first NCAA berth since WWII era
- Home-court dominance at Lavietes (long winning streak during this stretch)

If you want, I can add a game-by-game summary, full roster with stats, or all Ivy/postseason awards.
